items.name: Northview Center (Park Board senior programs and SeniorAge Northview Senior Center)
items.what: Senior programs for ages 55 and older include fitness, dance and dance lessons, arts and crafts, billiards, computers, choir, bingo, a book exchange, concerts, holiday events and field trips. SeniorAge serves an in-house lunch on weekdays.
items.access: Home of the Park Board Accessible Recreation program; call 417-837-5808 at least one week ahead to request activity modifications.
items.cost: No membership fee; some programs have nominal fees. SeniorAge lunch listed at $4 for age 60 and older, $8 under 60.
items.schedule: Monday through Friday

items.schedule: Weekdays; call the center or check SeniorAge menus page for current schedule.

items.name: The Library Center
items.what: District headquarters with a glass-enclosed reading room and art gallery, local history and genealogy collections, a 150-seat auditorium, outdoor patio and gift shop; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch. Has a motorized scooter for visitors with limited mobility, a video magnifier in the Local History Department, drive-up service, and a universal adult-size changing table in the Hatch Auditorium family restroom.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: The Library Station
items.what: A large branch with a comfortable reading room, meeting rooms and a Panera Bread cafe; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch. Has a wheelchair and an electric scooter for visitors with limited mobility; drive-up service.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Midtown Carnegie Branch Library
items.what: A restored 1905 Carnegie library with wooden library tables and comfortable reading chairs; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Schweitzer Brentwood Branch Library
items.what: A southeast Springfield branch near Battlefield Mall and Brentwood Center; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch. Drive-up service.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Republic Branch Library
items.what: New branch opened in 2026 with a 150-seat community room, Maker Space and an outdoor patio connected to a walking path with a StoryWalk; book discussions are listed.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch. Drive-up service.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Willard Branch Library
items.what: A neighborhood branch in the East Shopping Center on Jackson Street; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch. Drive-up service.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Ash Grove Branch Library
items.address: 101 E. Main St., Ash Grove, MO 65604
items.what: The district's oldest county branch (opened 1940), a small-town library where staff know many patrons by name; book discussions are listed.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Fair Grove Branch Library
items.address: 81 S. Orchard Blvd., Fair Grove, MO 65648
items.what: Branch inside the Fair Grove City Hall building; book discussions are listed for this branch.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Strafford Branch Library
items.what: An automobile-themed branch within view of Old Route 66, with vintage car murals, in Chestnut Plaza.
items.access: Magnifying glasses available at every branch.
items.cost: Free to visit; library programs listed as free unless noted.
items.schedule: Open daily or most days; see branch hours page. Book discussions listed per branch.

items.name: Christian County Library, Ozark Community Branch
items.what: Borrow books, audiobooks and DVDs and attend free library events; the events calendar can be filtered for programs for adults 18 and older.
items.cost: Library events listed as free; some require registration.
items.schedule: Open most days; see locations page.

items.name: Christian County Library, Nixa Community Branch
items.what: Borrow books and media and attend free library events, with an events calendar searchable by branch and age group.
items.cost: Library events listed as free; some require registration.
items.schedule: Open most days; see locations page.

items.name: Christian County Library, Clever Community Branch
items.what: Borrow books and media and attend free library events at this branch.
items.cost: Library events listed as free; some require registration.
items.schedule: Monday through Saturday; closed Sunday.

items.name: Christian County Library, Sparta Community Branch
items.what: Borrow books and media and attend free library events at this branch.
items.cost: Library events listed as free; some require registration.
items.schedule: See locations page for days.

items.name: Polk County Library, Rayl Family Library (Bolivar)
items.what: Adult programs include Sit and Stretch chair yoga designed for seniors, American Mahjong, a fiber arts group, Diamond Painting Club, arts and crafts classes, movies and several book clubs.
items.cost: Programs for ages 18 and up; some crafts require registration. Free homebound book delivery is available to residents of some Bolivar nursing homes.
items.schedule: Monday through Saturday; chair yoga listed every Wednesday.

items.name: Polk County Library, Fair Play Library
items.address: 104 N. Elm St., Fair Play, MO 65649
items.what: Hosts the History Repeats Itself historical fiction book club with coffee and dessert, a knitting and fiber arts group, and a mystery book chat.
items.cost: Free library programs.
items.schedule: Tuesday through Saturday.

items.name: Polk County Library, Humansville Library
items.what: Offers monthly take-home craft kits with supplies included and Tuesday night movies.
items.cost: Free library programs.
items.schedule: Monday through Saturday.

items.name: Webster County Library, Garst Memorial Library
items.what: Borrow books, audiobooks and movies, use Webster County newspaper microfilm, and check the library events calendar.
items.schedule: See library website for hours.

items.name: Webster County Library, Rogersville Branch
items.what: Borrow books and media and check the library events calendar.
items.schedule: See library website for hours.

items.name: Springfield Botanical Gardens at Nathanael Greene/Close Memorial Park
items.what: Tour themed gardens (rose, iris, peony, hosta, daylily, sensory and more), visit the Botanical Center gift shop and reference library, and see the Roston Native Butterfly House, Missouri's only native butterfly house.
items.access: The 6-mile paved South Creek Greenway runs through the park and suits wheelchairs and strollers.
items.cost: Grounds free. Butterfly House admission is free.
items.schedule: Grounds sunrise to sunset daily; Botanical Center open Monday through Saturday and Sunday afternoons; Butterfly House mid-May through September, weather permitting.

items.name: Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden
items.what: A 7.5-acre Japanese garden with meandering paths, a koi lake, moon bridge, tea house and meditation garden, created with sister city Isesaki, Japan.
items.access: The 0.51-mile main pathway is level stamped concrete with benches, suitable for wheelchairs; a few complimentary wheelchairs are available first come, and one motorized wheelchair can be rented for $15 for up to two hours (reserve at 417-891-1515); accessible parking near the entrance (path and wheelchair details per the Friends of the Garden Gardens Aglow page).
items.cost: $6 adults, $4 children 3 to 11.
items.schedule: April through October; closed November through March except special events.

items.name: Springfield Conservation Nature Center
items.address: Southeast Springfield just west of Highway 65 off the James River Freeway (Highway 60); follow brown signs
items.what: A 79-acre Missouri Department of Conservation area with about three miles of hiking trails, a self-guided exhibit area, information desk, gift shop and bird watching.
items.cost: No admission listed.
items.schedule: Grounds open daily; building open Tuesday through Saturday, closed Sunday, Monday and some holidays.

items.name: Phelps Grove Park
items.what: A historic 30-acre park with mature trees, a paved walking track, a formal flower garden with a shade structure, the Victims' Memorial Garden and several sculptures.
items.access: Paved walking track.
items.cost: Free city park.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: Lake Springfield Park and Boathouse
items.what: 158 acres with more than a mile of shoreline, a paved 1.74-mile trail with several fishing areas, wildlife watching (eagles in winter) and a boathouse with a gift shop and restrooms.
items.access: Paved trail; accessible parking at the Boathouse.
items.cost: Free park. Boathouse is cash-free; canoe and kayak rentals are extra.
items.schedule: Year-round; boat rentals May 1 through August 31.

items.name: Valley Water Mill Park
items.address: 2400 E Valley Water Mill Road, Springfield, MO
items.what: Fish a 13-acre lake stocked with bass, bluegill and catfish from accessible piers, or walk the boardwalk and 1.5-mile lake trail.
items.access: Boardwalks and fishing piers are fully accessible; restrooms in the Watershed Committee building.
items.cost: Free park.
items.schedule: Open daily dawn to dusk; best fishing late fall and early spring.

items.name: South Creek Greenway (Ozark Greenways)
items.address: Trailhead at McDaniel Park, National Avenue and Sunset Street, Springfield
items.what: A paved east-west trail through Springfield linking to Nathanael Greene/Close Memorial Park and the Botanical Center, with a bird-rich section along Sunset Street.
items.access: Mixed asphalt and concrete paved surface with minimal to moderate inclines; suited to wheelchairs and strollers.
items.cost: Free.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: Frisco Highline Trail, Willard Trailhead
items.address: Willard Trailhead, Willard (trail runs 35 miles Springfield to Bolivar)
items.what: A scenic rail-trail with old railroad bridges, history kiosks (including Willard's 1908 bank robbery at mile 6) and transportation-themed sculptures.
items.cost: Free.
items.schedule: Year-round; Friday evening events at the Willard Trailhead from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

items.name: Finley River Park
items.what: A family-friendly city park by the Finley River with open space and three reservable picnic pavilions.
items.cost: Free park; pavilion rental extra.
items.schedule: Sunrise to sunset; may be closed in November and December for the Festival of Lights.

items.name: Gardens at Woodfield
items.what: A 6-acre botanical garden with a half-mile walking trail.
items.cost: Free city park.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: Dickerson Park Zoo
items.what: See over 500 animals from five continents, including the giraffe feeding deck, petting zoo and Titus Express miniature train.
items.cost: Adults $19; age 60 and older $16.
items.schedule: Open daily, weather permitting.

items.name: Wilson's Creek National Battlefield
items.address: 5242 S. State Hwy ZZ, Republic, MO 65738
items.what: Watch the museum film and exhibits in the visitor center, then drive the paved 4.9-mile one-way tour road with seven stops including the historic Ray House and Bloody Hill.
items.access: Visitor center and Ray House are wheelchair accessible from parking; a wheelchair is available in the visitor center; tour road stops are wheelchair accessible but trails off the road are primitive. Restrooms and water only at the visitor center.
items.cost: The park's 2026 Fees page says no entrance pass is required (an older tour road page mentions an entry fee; confirm at the visitor center).
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: History Museum on the Square
items.what: Eight interactive galleries on Springfield history, including a passenger train ride, Civil War and Wild Bill Hickok exhibits, and a Route 66 gallery with neon signs and a 1957 Chevy Bel Air.
items.access: Wheelchair accessible with an elevator to all floors; a manual wheelchair is available free; drop-off at the front, parking behind the museum.
items.cost: Adults $16; seniors $13.
items.schedule: Wednesday through Sunday; closed Monday and Tuesday.

items.name: Air and Military Museum of the Ozarks
items.what: A hands-on military history museum with over 5,000 pieces of military memorabilia and restored vintage equipment; volunteers greet visitors and lead tours.
items.access: Listed as wheelchair accessible by VisitMO.
items.cost: Admission charged; members free.
items.schedule: Tuesday through Saturday afternoons; groups by appointment.

items.name: Johnny Morris' Wonders of Wildlife National Museum and Aquarium
items.what: A large wildlife gallery and aquarium attraction next to Bass Pro Shops; a local Just For Neighbors discount and weekday afternoon discount are offered.
items.access: Wheelchair accessible and stroller friendly with elevators throughout and seating in galleries; electric scooters rent for $25 at ticket counters.
items.cost: Paid admission; see tickets page for local discounts.
items.schedule: Open daily; Sea of Lights holiday display begins November 1.

items.name: Discovery Center of Springfield (with grandkids)
items.address: 438 E St. Louis St., Springfield, MO 65806
items.what: A hands-on science center with 15 galleries on six floors, including animatronic dinosaurs, a walk-through giant eyeball and a real aircraft cockpit; good for visits with grandchildren.
items.cost: Adults (16+) $17; children 3 to 15 $12.
items.schedule: Tuesday through Sunday; closed Monday.

items.name: Webster County Historical Museum
items.what: A local history museum in Marshfield's former Carnegie Library, open since 1997, with an annex holding newspaper archives and probate records for family research.
items.access: Listed by VisitMO as not wheelchair accessible.
items.schedule: Check website for hours.

items.name: Nathan and Olive Boone Homestead State Historic Site
items.address: 7850 N. State Highway V, Ash Grove, MO 65604
items.what: Explore the 1830s last home of Nathan Boone, youngest son of Daniel Boone, and the associated cemeteries.
items.schedule: Year-round; see site page.

items.name: Springfield Little Theatre at the Historic Landers Theatre
items.what: A volunteer-driven community theatre staging plays and musicals in the historic Landers Theatre; the theatre also hosts Springfield Ballet's Nutcracker.
items.cost: Ticketed.
items.schedule: Fall through spring season; see show calendar.

items.name: Gillioz Center for Arts and Entertainment
items.what: A historic nonprofit theatre presenting concerts, classic films such as its Fall Classics series, and touring shows.
items.cost: Ticketed.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: Springfield Symphony Orchestra, Seniors at the Symphony
items.address: Juanita K. Hammons Hall for the Performing Arts, 525 S. John Q. Hammons Parkway, Springfield, MO 65802
items.what: Seniors at the Symphony is an outreach program offering seniors discounted tickets with full transportation to a live symphony concert.
items.access: Transportation is included in the program.
items.cost: Discounted tickets.
items.schedule: A November 2026 concert has a waitlist; call 417-864-6683.

items.name: Chesterfield Family Center (Park Board)
items.what: SilverSneakers classes, an indoor walking track, pickleball, and an indoor aquatic center with a whirlpool spa, resistance walk and zero-depth entry pool.
items.cost: SilverSneakers members (65+ on eligible Medicare plans) get free family center membership; day passes available.
items.schedule: Year-round; SilverSneakers classes on weekdays.

items.name: Doling Family Center and Indoor Aquatic Center (Park Board)
items.what: SilverSneakers classes, indoor walking track, pickleball, low-impact water fitness, lap lanes open for lane walking, and a therapeutic whirlpool spa, in historic Doling Park.
items.cost: SilverSneakers members (65+ on eligible Medicare plans) get free family center membership; day passes available.
items.schedule: Year-round; SilverSneakers classes on weekdays.

items.name: Dan Kinney Family Center (Park Board)
items.what: SilverSneakers classes, pickleball and a 1/16-mile indoor walking track, located in Dan Kinney Park.
items.cost: SilverSneakers members (65+ on eligible Medicare plans) get free family center membership; day passes available.
items.schedule: Year-round; SilverSneakers classes on weekdays.

items.name: Southwest Missouri Senior Games
items.address: Northview Center, 305 E. Talmage Street, Springfield, MO 65803
items.what: Lifetime sports competition and socializing for athletes 50 and up, with events such as billiards, archery, track and field and golf.
items.cost: Registration required; details vary per event.
items.schedule: Spring (registration for billiards, archery and track and field posted).

items.name: Pat Jones YMCA
items.what: Active Older Adults programs including SilverSneakers classes for range of motion, coordination and balance, and water fitness classes for low-impact strength and flexibility.
items.cost: Accepts SilverSneakers, Renew Active and Silver and Fit Medicare plans for possible free membership; financial assistance available.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: The X Center (Nixa Parks and Recreation)
items.address: McCauley Park, off North St. and Taylor Way, Nixa, MO
items.what: Nixa Parks headquarters with a fitness center, aquatics center and indoor gym in 40-acre McCauley Park.
items.schedule: Year-round.

items.name: Farmers Market of the Ozarks
items.address: 2144 E. Republic Road, Springfield, MO (Farmers Park)
items.what: Shop local produce and artisan gifts, hear local musicians and have breakfast or lunch in a laid-back market setting.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Saturdays year-round (later winter opening).

items.name: Greater Springfield Farmers' Market
items.address: 2825 S. Glenstone Ave Ste 101, Springfield, MO (Battlefield Mall)
items.what: Springfield's original farmers market, where every vendor grows, harvests or makes what they sell; over 50 local vendors.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Saturdays year-round; Tuesdays and Thursdays April through October.

items.name: Ozark Farmers Market at Finley Farms
items.what: An evening market with live music, food trucks and fresh local produce.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Thursdays May through September.

items.name: Nixa Area Farmers Market
items.what: Locally grown produce and handcrafted goods in downtown Nixa.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Saturdays May through September.

items.name: Greater Polk County Farmers' Market
items.what: Local farmers and craftsmen selling fresh produce and locally sourced products.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Tuesdays and Saturdays in season.

items.name: Ozark Empire Fair
items.what: Southwest Missouri's large annual county-style fair with livestock, food, rides and grandstand shows.
items.access: The fairgrounds site lists a Mobility Scooters/Wheelchairs visitor page.
items.cost: No senior discount, but anyone over 80 gets in free; a $3 day was offered in 2026.
items.schedule: Late July into early August (2026: July 30 to August 8).

items.name: Harvest Fest and Pumpkin Patch at Rutledge-Wilson Farm Park
items.what: A fall tradition with hayrides, a pumpkin patch, gourds for sale, a corn maze and food trucks.
items.cost: Free admission; most activities have a small fee.
items.schedule: Late September through October.

items.name: Japanese Fall Festival at Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden
items.what: An annual festival in the Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden; the Park Board held public input sessions there in 2026.
items.access: See Mizumoto item for paved path and wheelchair details.
items.schedule: September (2026: September 12 and 13).

items.name: Gardens Aglow
items.address: Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden, 2400 S. Scenic Ave., Springfield, MO 65807
items.what: Walk a botanical-themed holiday light festival with more than 225,000 lights in the Japanese garden, with fire pits and hot drinks for sale.
items.access: Paved, lit, level stamped concrete paths with benches; complimentary wheelchairs first come; motorized wheelchair rental $15 (reserve 417-891-1515); accessible parking.
items.cost: Ticketed; tickets on sale October 31; Friends of the Garden members free.
items.schedule: Late November through December (closed Christmas Eve and Christmas Day).

items.name: First Friday Art Walk
items.address: Downtown Springfield and Commercial Street Historic District
items.what: A free, self-guided evening tour of local galleries, art, music and food run by the Springfield Regional Arts Council.
items.cost: Free.
items.schedule: First Friday of every month.

items.name: Nixa Sucker Days
items.what: A festival dating to 1957 with arts, crafts and food vendors, a parade, live music and free samples of fried suckerfish.
items.schedule: May (2026: May 15 and 16).

items.name: Republic Pumpkin Daze
items.what: A free fall festival with nearly 400 food and craft vendors, giant pumpkins and produce, and Kiwanis bingo in a new pavilion.
items.access: News report notes a new flat parking lot and walking trails at the park.
items.cost: Free.
items.schedule: Early October (2026: October 2 and 3).

items.name: Apple Butter Makin' Days (day trip)
items.what: Watch and help stir apple butter cooked in copper kettles over open fires on the courthouse lawn, with a parade, contests, music and hundreds of vendor booths.
items.schedule: October (second weekend).

items.name: Silver Dollar City Harvest Festival and An Old Time Christmas (day trip)
items.address: 399 Silver Dollar City Pkwy, Branson, MO 65616
items.what: Seasonal festivals at the 1880s-themed park: visiting craftsmen and pumpkins in fall, and over 6.5 million lights, holiday shows and handcrafted gifts at Christmas.
items.access: Free parking with trams and buses to the entrance; an Accessibility Center offers downloadable guides on physical, visual, hearing and cognitive accommodations; rental services available.
items.cost: Ticketed theme park.
items.schedule: Harvest Festival through October 31; An Old Time Christmas November 7, 2026 to January 2, 2027.

items.name: Bass Pro Shops Outdoor World (flagship)
items.what: Browse the original store with seven large aquariums, an indoor swamp with alligators and turtles, wildlife displays and waterfalls; weekend fish feedings and an on-site restaurant.
items.cost: Free to browse.
items.schedule: Daily; fish feedings Friday through Sunday.

items.name: Lambert's Cafe, Home of Throwed Rolls
items.address: 1800 W. State Highway J, Ozark, MO 65721
items.what: A long-running family restaurant known for throwed rolls, country dishes such as chicken fried steak, and free pass-around sides.
items.cost: Restaurant prices.
items.schedule: Daily; call ahead for to-go orders.

items.name: Springfield-Greene County Library Volunteering
items.what: Volunteers age 14 and older help in gift shops, shelve materials, assist with the Walking Books program for homebound patrons, and help with clerical work; Friends of the Library run book sales.
items.cost: Unpaid.
items.schedule: As positions open.

items.name: SeniorAge Volunteer Program
items.what: Volunteer at a senior center front desk or lunch program, deliver meals to homebound older adults, lead classes or crafts, or join the Silver-Haired Legislature.
items.cost: Training provided; mileage reimbursement for meal delivery.
items.schedule: A few hours a month or week.

items.name: Friends of the Garden Volunteers (Springfield Botanical Gardens)
items.what: Adopt a garden section, be a Butterfly House docent, demonstrate heirloom arts at the Gray/Campbell Farmstead, or help at events.
items.cost: Unpaid.
items.schedule: Butterfly House May through September; Farmstead April through October.

items.name: Ozarks Food Harvest Sort and Pack
items.what: Volunteers sort, check and repack food during three-hour sessions at the O'Reilly Center for Hunger Relief; volunteers also assemble Senior Food Boxes.
items.cost: Unpaid; orientation provided; ages 12 and up.
items.schedule: Weekday sessions; monthly or weekly.

items.name: CoxHealth Volunteer Services
items.what: Volunteers staff information desks and gift shops and escort patients and visitors.
items.cost: Unpaid; interview, background, drug and immunization screening and orientation required.
items.schedule: Ongoing.
